faqs.a:
(a)
Any domestic bee colony not residing in a hive box intended for beekeeping, or any
               swarm of domestic bees, or any colony residing in a standard or homemade hive box
               which, by virtue of its condition, has obviously been abandoned by the beekeeper,
               is unlawful and may be summarily destroyed or removed from the city by the city manager
               or designee thereof. Summary destruction or removal from the city of any colony or
               hive box as set forth herein shall not preclude prosecution for any violation of this
               article.
(b)
Nothing in this article shall prevent the city manager or designee thereof from exercising
               his authority to summarily destroy, remove, or otherwise abate a swarm or colony of
               non-domestic bees or honeybees which is found or deemed to constitute a nuisance under
               article III of
chapter 38
of this Code.
(c)
In all cases where the city manager or his designee determines that summary destruction
               or removal of a swarm, colony, or hive box is necessary, 24 hours notice shall be
               given in writing, signed by the city manager or his designee, to the owner, agent,
               tenant, or occupant of such structure or premises to remove such swarm, colony, or
               hive box. In case of such person's neglect or refusal to abate the same in accordance
               with such notice, he shall be chargeable with the expenses which may be incurred in
               the abatement thereof, to be collected by suit or otherwise in accordance with
chapter 59
, municipal liens, of this Code and in addition to the penalty provided in this article
               for violation hereof.
(
Ord. No. 4345, § 1, 8-6-2012
)
